VIZ 23 — Overfitting: when a model memorizes instead of learning.

The intuition: you can drive training loss down by fitting a high-degree polynomial (or a large neural net) to the quirks of your dataset. But if you only check train error, you miss the failure mode: test error rises because the model learned noise, not the underlying signal.

Under the hood (production view):
- Train vs test vs validation: Training loss can improve continuously while generalization degrades.
- Evaluation loop: Always gate model selection on validation metrics; reserve test for final reporting.
- Overfitting signals: large train–test gap, unstable performance across time splits, and brittleness to distribution shift.

When you connect this to modern AI agent architectures:
- Vector embeddings similarity search helps agents retrieve relevant context, but retrieval quality can mask overfitting elsewhere.
- Autonomous ai agents architecture still needs robust offline eval + online monitoring; “it works for my prompts” is not evaluation.
- LLM system design best practice: treat embeddings/agents as components—measure retrieval hit-rate, downstream task success, and calibration separately.

Trade-offs & patterns:
- Regularization + early stopping: cheaper than constantly collecting more data.
- Data strategy: augmentation and better sampling often beat larger models.
- Safer rollouts: use canary deployments and track test-like metrics continuously.
